newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian, U.S. spacemen begin space walk.
newsitem.headline: Russian, U.S. spacemen begin space walk.

text.p: A Russian cosmonaut and a U.S. astronaut stepped out of the orbiting station Mir on Tuesday at the start of a space walk due to last about six hours, a mission control spokesman said.

"Vasiliy Tsibliev and NASA astronaut Jerry Linenger left Mir at 9.10 a.m. Moscow time (0510 GMT) and started work in outer space," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone from the control centre in the town of Korolyov, outside Moscow.
The spacewalk had been due to begin 20 minutes earlier but the spokesman did not explain the delay.
He said the two men would dismantle equipment which collects samples of space dust outside the station.

"The cosmonauts will bring in a few devices which were installed outside Mir in March 1996," the spokesman said, adding that the devices would be brought to Earth by the U.S. Shuttle spacecraft next month.
Mission control had radio and visual contact with Linenger and Tsibliev, he said. "The third Mir cosmonaut -- Alexander Lazutkin -- is videotaping his colleagues' work from the station."
